videos.title: What Your Brain Does When Your Crush Texts Back #shorts
videos.description:
Your crush just texted back. Here's what your brain just did: suspense, a dopamine reward hit, adrenaline butterflies, and why you keep rereading it.

The Crush Files: real science of crushes, every Friday.

📚 Sources
- Aron, Fisher et al. (2005), J Neurophysiol: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15928068/
- Fiorillo, Tobler & Schultz (2003), Science: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/12649484/
- Marazziti et al. (1999), Psychological Medicine: https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/psychological-medicine/article/alteration-of-the-platelet-serotonin-transporter-in-romantic-love/9599BA293019DFA6D05B315803B6D2A7
- The Conversation: why we get butterflies: https://theconversation.com/explainer-why-do-we-get-butterflies-in-our-stomachs-72232

Narration uses an AI voice. Animation and music are original.

videos.title: You're About Half Bacteria #shorts
videos.description:
The famous "10 bacteria for every human cell" came from a 1972 back-of-the-envelope estimate. The 2016 recount: about 38 trillion vs 30 trillion. One trip to the toilet can tip the balance.

Full story: "What If All Your Bacteria Suddenly Vanished?" on the channel.

📚 Sources
- Sender et al. 2016, PLOS Biology: https://journals.plos.org/plosbiology/article?id=10.1371/journal.pbio.1002533
- Boston Globe 2014: https://www.bostonglobe.com/ideas/2014/09/13/your-body-mostly-microbes-actually-have-idea/qlcoKot4wfUXecjeVaFKFN/story.html
- Science News: https://www.sciencenews.org/article/bodys-bacteria-dont-outnumber-human-cells-so-much-after-all

Narration uses an AI voice. Animation and music are original.
